extracted.intended_audience: aspiring and practicing writers, storytellers, and fiction authors
extracted.subtask_description: A single-author list of 25 concise principles and heuristics for crafting stories, covering structure, character, pacing, voice, and purpose aimed at improving narrative impact. Practical, general guidance for fiction and narrative writing across media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories Have Power
rubrics_metrics.description: "Stories move the world at the same time they explain our place in it."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize storytelling's capacity to shape thought, feeling, and culture; use that power responsibly and deliberately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect Above Entertainment
rubrics_metrics.description: Superior narratives create emotional impact beyond simple amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize emotional or thematic effect over merely amusing the audience; aim to move readers, not just distract them.

rubrics_metrics.name: A Good Story Is Good Regardless Of Genre Or Form
rubrics_metrics.description: Quality transcends medium.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A well-told story works across genres and formats — focus on fundamentals of craft rather than genre constraints alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form Still Matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Each medium has organic constraints shaping how stories function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the specific affordances and limits of the chosen medium (novel, short story, film, etc.) when making storytelling choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stories Have Shape, Even Unintentionally
rubrics_metrics.description: All narratives possess structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of implicit shapes and structures in your work; even unintended structure affects pacing, meaning, and reader response.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Story Is A Map; Plot Is The Route
rubrics_metrics.description: Story = world/characters/atmosphere; plot = sequence chosen within.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish the broader world and thematic territory (the map) from the specific events you select and order (the route); both matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality In Plot vs. Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Plot elements repeat across narratives; unique arrangement creates original stories (LEGO blocks metaphor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Originality often comes from recombining familiar parts in new ways rather than inventing wholly novel raw materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Bridge Between Author And Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Readers seek connection and self-recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write to establish empathy and resonance; give readers something to recognize themselves in or to care about.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge The Audience
rubrics_metrics.description: Great storytellers respectfully defy expectations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Push readers' expectations and assumptions, but do so fairly — surprising yet earned choices deepen engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Tale Survives Without Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: "Conflict is the food that feeds the reader."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure meaningful conflict drives the story; stakes and opposition are central to sustaining interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance Tension and Release
rubrics_metrics.description: Narrative builds through pressure punctuated by relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage beats of tension and respite so the reader experiences momentum without fatigue; alternate build and catharsis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peaks, Valleys, and Varied Pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful narratives avoid linear progression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vary pacing and scene intensity — create rises and dips to maintain engagement rather than a flat, constant tempo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell Only The Story
rubrics_metrics.description: Eliminate digressions that distract from core themes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove elements that don't serve the narrative's purpose; be ruthless about trimming extraneous material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Big Ideas Need Small Spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstract concepts resonate through individual character experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anchor large themes in concrete, personal moments; show ideas through the particular rather than tell them abstractly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Backstory Requires Delicate Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Excessive exposition overwhelms readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Integrate backstory sparingly and organically; avoid info-dumps and let history reveal itself through action, dialogue, and consequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Characters Drive The Narrative
rubrics_metrics.description: Without interesting people, narratives lose engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize compelling character development — motivations, desires, and change are what push plot and theme forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Villains Have Mothers
rubrics_metrics.description: Antagonists possess humanity and motivations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give antagonists believable reasons, depth, and sympathy where appropriate; avoid one-dimensional evil.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heroes Have Broken Toys
rubrics_metrics.description: Protagonists benefit from flaws and moral complexity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make protagonists imperfect and conflicted; their vulnerabilities create drama and reader investment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strip Skin Off Bones
rubrics_metrics.description: Study narrative mechanics by crafting minimal stories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practice with stripped-down tales to learn structure and mechanics — simpler exercises illuminate craft fundamentals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beginnings Are For Assholes
rubrics_metrics.description: Start narratives late; engage readers where action emerges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid prolonged setup; open near or at the inciting incident to hook readers quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't Jump Too Deep Too Fast
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences need emotional anchors before dramatic intensity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build empathy and context before subjecting characters (and readers) to extreme events; balance immediacy with grounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat Place Like Character
rubrics_metrics.description: Settings should seem alive and significant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use setting to influence mood, plot, and character behavior — make place integral rather than decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Always Ask Why You Tell This
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowing your tether to material strengthens delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be explicit with yourself about the story's purpose and why this particular tale matters; that clarity informs choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: It's Okay To Bury The Lede
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtext allows deeper meaning beneath surface.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trust readers to read between the lines; use implication and subtext to yield richer interpretive layers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Writing Is Craft, Storytelling Is Art
rubrics_metrics.description: Storytelling transcends mechanics into artistic expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Master technical craft, but aim beyond technique toward artistry that evokes feeling and meaning.
